title: Brunch
subtitle: This gap—fill it up with tangible things, like warm hugs and heartfelt embraces.

trails.title: Life's Essentials
trails.description: A compilation of potion recipes from popular books such as the Common Household Potions Handbook and Anyone Can Be An Alchemist: Simple and Easy Brewing Techniques.

content.text:
Lubricating Ointment

Snail mucus, acacia sap (scraped), swiftlet saliva, vulture feather powder.

—Vulture feather powder is hard to come by, and from the looks of it, it is not an essential ingredient.

—Swiftlet saliva, however, is absolutely required.

—Lanolin snails yield the best results.

Sleeping Draught

Hairy agrimony and elm leaves (crushed), oranges (juiced), winter bear's paw (fur dried in blue twilight), coarse salt.

—Remember to buy hairy agrimony seeds Bought.

—Too much salt drastically affects both the taste and sleep induction.

Special Pain Relief Balm

Olive oil, Ead's tongue (soaked in cold water), petrified resin (softened), white crystal, dragon bone powder

—Dragon bone? For everyday use?! Of course I can afford that! I'll just trade up fifty bottles of regular balm for one meager ounce of dragon bone powder, why bloody not? It is such a bargain!

—Alternative substitute: ... Or, just use fifty bottles of regular balm and endure the pain until it subsides.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: The Floor Ritual is one of the most popular events of the Uluru Games. It has a bewitching style that generates a resonance between the dancer and audience.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Charlotte was a genius. She was born for it. And God has sent her a coach covered in dark feathers and skilled in ancient Celtic runes.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Coach Raven taught her the primal witch dance that ignited a fire within her. At least, until that tragedy 10 years ago which took her leg.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Coach Raven had given her a pocket of flower seeds as a reward for all her diligent practicing. It's said they were from the druids in the forests of Glastonbury.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: I guess she planted them around her house and got this garden. Now all these bizarre plants share the same strange air with their owner.
The plants in the mansion's garden are all drooping toward the ground. There is a new sense of weariness that wasn't present during Tooth Fairy's last visit.
The woman by the door gently shakes her head as Flutterpage crawls around on her knees, searching for bugs among the foliage.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Thank you again for having me over. That's all I have to say about Charlotte.
Flutterpage's head pops out from between the plants.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: What's a druid? Is it a place? Do they have canaries and snails there?

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: A druid isn't a place. It's a title, an identity.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Identity. Oh, like a name, just like Flutterpage, right?
She quickly falls back into her own musings.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Thank you for your cooperation, Ms. Bartley. I'm sorry to be taking you away from your practice.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Yes, you should be. I don't much enjoy being bothered by stuffed-up bureaucrats.
The accomplished Floor Ritualist has never been one to hold back her words.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: But if you ask me—
Caroline glances once more at the narrow window of the old Victorian house. It's tightly shut.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: I will tell you that it isn't Charlotte that's summoning the black fog.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: I stand by that. I swear it on all my honor as an Uluru competitor.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: We're witches, but not in the traditional sense. We practice witchcraft to win medals instead of summoning devils.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: We trust you at your word. It seems like that concludes our investigation into this Fog Hag. Thanks again, Ms. Bartley.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Ms. Tooth Fairy, if you do want to thank me, mind doing me a favor?
Tooth Fairy nods, but Caroline seems to have an unusual hesitation as she deliberates over her choice of words.
In the end, she yields.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Please do something, anything, to bring her out of this hole she's dug for herself.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Whatever you do, break down her door, drag her out by her hair, even blow up that old mansion.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Just don't let her hide in her stupid house.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: She'll let you inside now. There's no longer any power preventing you. I can sense it.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Hmm. You know this place well. Have you visited her here before?
Caroline bites her lip, holding back the words on the tip of her tongue.
Then, she walks away.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I think Ms. Bartley wants to come in with us.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Maybe so, but she's made her choice. She doesn't want to join us inside.
Tooth Fairy shakes the jar in her hand, not containing her usual toothfairies but filled with a collection of lanolin snails.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Let's go, Flutterpage. We still have work to do.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Whatever you say, Ms. Witch Doctor.
The two of them step cautiously into the garden, the soil compacting under their feet. There is nothing left to obstruct their path.
They step around a few threatening-looking plants as they take the winding road to the creaky oak door.
Tooth Fairy goes to knock, but the door swings open the moment her knuckle hits its surface.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Ah! The door isn't locked. Let's get inside.
Willow sits at the table prepared for one, surrounded by an exorbitant amount of half-finished food.
Aside from the full English she's currently tucking into, there's a scotch egg, a half-eaten cod and chips, and a steaming apple crumble.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Sorry to interrupt.
Willow casts aside basic manners, neglecting to invite her guests to sit, and cuts herself another piece of sausage.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: *swallow*

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Diets high in sugar and fatty oils may well lead to stomach illness, Ms. O'Hagan.
She continues to eat her lavish brunch.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: I choose the name, Tooth Fairy, instead of my real name, Campbell. But did you choose to let people call you Willow?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Or, do you prefer the name Charlotte O'Hagan?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: That is the name of ... an excellent Uluru Floor Ritualist.
The crash of silverware interrupts her once more.
Then, Willow sweeps her arm across the table.
The silver dishes clatter loudly as they fly to the floor.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Tooth Fairy, some kind of doctor, right? I think your prescription is a little fuzzy. I'm no athlete. I've only got one leg.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: This Charlotte has nothing to do with Willow.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Just like I've nothing to do with the Uluru Games.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: So far as I know, the Uluru Games do not exclude people with disabilities from full participation.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: To be sure, but only if you enjoy parading yourself around for embarrassment. I think I'll pass, thanks.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: No one should feel embarrassed by competing, least of all the competitors challenging themselves. That is the point of the Uluru spirit.
Willow rises with great effort, furiously stamping the floor with her prosthesis in the process.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Excuse me? I don't remember having asked you for a running commentary.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: I'm sure you already know the answer in your heart. You have wisdom and experience.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Who even invited you here?! It's time you leave.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: I'm here representing our mutual friend, Flutterpage.
At the mention of this name, Willow pauses and takes a step back.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: What for?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: I understand that usually the only one welcome inside is Flutterpage, but I'm here to apologize on her behalf.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Apologize?
She places a small jar of snails on the table.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: What's this?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: An apology gift. She ran off a little before sunrise to collect these for you.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: She collects these arcane creatures you use to make the lubricant for your prosthesis, right?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: But she's afraid that you'll get angry at her again, so she asked me to give it to you.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Oh, I see. Now I'm the hateful, angry, wicked witch.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: No, you're not. The things that these people say about you, they aren't true.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: As I mentioned, Flutterpage wanted to apologize, because, quote, she "didn't want to break your heart."

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Ms. Bartley has told her many things about you. She never knew you're such an outstanding competitor.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Caroline?
Tooth Fairy slowly pushes the jar of snails closer to her.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: So, will you accept her gift?
Willow delicately places her fingertips on the jar, neither pushing it away nor taking it.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Ugh, nosy little brat.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Where is she now? In the temporary hospital?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: You want to see her?
The witch's features twist like a knot.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Don't push me!
She pulls the snail jar closer to her.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Alright, it's my own fault! I shouldn't have treated her that way!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: That what you wanted to hear, is it?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Fine, then. You'll have what you want. Just take me to her!

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: She's waiting by the door.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: What?
Flutterpage cautiously peeks out from the edge of the doorframe, her wide eyes scanning the room for any sign of danger.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Willow?
At this point, there is no turning back.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Fine! Come on in then.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: *sob*
Unable to deal with her emotions, tears well up in Flutterpage's eyes once again.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Stop your crying.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Listen, I—

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Urgh, I ...

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I shouldn't have treated you so wickedly the last time, and the time before that.
Tooth Fairy gives a silent nod.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Now would you stop that crying? At least not here in my—

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: *crying*
Without a moment's hesitation, Flutterpage charges toward her.
Willow's hands open and close like a spider raising its front legs in fear.
She's not sure whether she can catch this chaotic bundle of rags.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Oi!
*bang*
She manages to catch her, only to be knocked back to the floor.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I'm sorry ... I-I'm really very sorry ...

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Tsk ...

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I swear I won't break into your house no more. I'll only come in when you let me.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I'll do anythin' you ask, say anythin' you need me to say, Miss.
She unconsciously looks to Tooth Fairy, only to see that her full attention is directed at the Uluru Floor Ritual painting on the wall.
Willow gently taps the back of Flutterpage's neck through several layers of old clothing.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: So, could I still come around again sometime?
Willow presses her hand to the girl's mouth, stifling her sobs.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Wumm.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Stop your crying first, lass.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Okay! I'll stop cryin'.
With a soft push, Flutterpage drifts into the air like a sheet caught in the wind.
Even with the removal of Flutterpage's weight, Willow is left on the floor, unable to get up.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Let ... Can I help you?
Flutterpage moves closer, reaching out both hands in line with Willow's.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Heh.
She takes the offered hands and rises steadily, the sudden gust of wind helping her find her balance.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Enough, enough. I've had too much of this for one day.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Would you mind if I politely asked you to leave?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: You do have a black fog to chase after all, don't you?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Just so you know, it truly has nothing to do with me.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. O'Hagan ...

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Call me Willow, child. What else do you want to say?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Would you let the food stay in your tummy for a bit longer? Eat a little more. I don't want you to be so skinny.
Willow pries Flutterpage's arm from around her waist, gently pushing her back.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Alright. Now leave me be, please.
Tooth Fairy takes Flutterpage's hand, and, as they leave the room, the old house sinks back into silence. There is no sound save for the heavy ticking of the grandfather clock.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: She's seen too much of this embarrassing side of me.
